paragraphs: CTS Corporation ("CTS", "we", "our", "us" or the "Company") is a global manufacturer of sensors, connectivity components, and actuators. CTS was established in 1896 as a provider of high-quality telephone products and was incorporated as an Indiana corporation in February 1929. Our principal executive offices are located in Lisle, Illinois.

We design, manufacture, and sell a broad line of sensors, connectivity components, and actuators primarily to original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs"), tier one suppliers for the aerospace and defense, industrial, medical, and transportation markets, and the U.S. Government. Our vision is to be a leading provider of sensing and motion devices as well as connectivity components, enabling an intelligent and seamless world. These devices are categorized by their ability to Sense, Connect or Move. Sense products provide vital inputs to electronic systems. Connect products allow systems to function in synchronization with other systems. Move products ensure required movements are effectively and accurately executed. We are committed to achieving our vision by continuing to invest in the development of products, technologies, and talent within these categories.

We operate manufacturing facilities in North America, Asia, and Europe. Sales and marketing are accomplished through our sales engineers. We also utilize independent manufacturers' representatives and distributors to extend our sales capability.
See the Consolidated Financial Statements and Notes included in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for financial information regarding the Company.

Our products perform specific electronic functions for a given product family and are intended for use in products assembled by our customers. The following table identifies major products by industry. Products are sold to industry OEMs, tier one suppliers, distributors and the U.S. Government.
Industrial Medical Aerospace and Defense SENSE (Controls, Pedals, Piezo Sensing Products, Sensors,
Switches, Transducers) CONNECT (EMI/RFI Filters, Capacitors, Frequency Control Products, Resistors, RF filters)

Sales and marketing to customers is accomplished through our sales engineers, independent manufacturers' representatives, and distributors. We maintain sales offices in China, Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, Japan, Singapore, Taiwan, and the United States. Approximately 86% of 2025 net sales were attributable to our sales engineers.

Our sales engineers generally service our largest customers with application-specific products. The vast majority of our products are engineered solutions. The sales engineers work closely with major customers in designing and developing products to meet specific customer requirements.

In 2025, independent distributors accounted for approximately 7% of net sales. We use distributors for a small portion of our product portfolio that are standard and require less design support, to service smaller customers, and to provide supply chain fulfillment for certain customers. Our key distribution partners include large global and regional distributors such as Avnet, Inc., Digi-Key Electronics, Master Electronics, Future Electronics, and TTI, Inc. In addition, we also utilize the services of independent manufacturers' representatives for customers not serviced directly by our sales engineers. Independent manufacturers' representatives receive commissions from us in exchange for their services. During 2025, approximately 7% of net sales were attributable to independent manufacturers' representatives.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
Our customers may cancel their orders, change production quantities or locations or delay production.

Our business, financial condition and results of operations could be adversely affected by disruptions in the global economy caused by the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict or other geopolitical tensions and conflict.
The impacts of supply chain constraints, increased tariffs and inflationary pressures could adversely impact our operating results.
We sell products to customers in cyclical industries that are subject to significant downturns that could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and operating results.
We are susceptible to trends and factors affecting industries that we serve.
Our operating results may vary significantly from period to period.
We may restructure our operations or fail to execute capital projects as planned, which may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and operating results.
We have a substantial amount of goodwill on our balance sheet. Future write-offs of goodwill may have the effect of decreasing our earnings or increasing our losses.
We may be unable to compete effectively against competitors.
We may be unable to keep pace with rapid technological changes that could make some of our products or processes obsolete before we realize a return on our investment.
Products we manufacture may contain design or manufacturing defects that could result in reduced demand for our products or services and liability claims against us.
We are subject to government regulations, including environmental, health, and safety laws and regulations, that expose us to potential financial liability.
Changes in tax laws could cause volatility or have a material adverse effect on our business and financial results.
Uncertainty over global tariffs and trade policies, or the financial impact of tariffs and trade policies, may negatively affect our results.

As we integrate artificial intelligence technologies into our processes, these technologies may present business, compliance and reputational risks.

paragraphs: The following are certain risk factors that could affect our business, financial condition and operating results. These risk factors should be considered in connection with evaluating forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K or in any other reports filed or furnished by us, because these factors could cause our actual results and financial condition to differ materially from those projected in any such forward-looking statements. Before you invest in us, you should know that making such an investment involves risks, including the risks described below. Although the risks are organized by headings, and each risk is discussed separately, many are interrelated. The risks that are highlighted below are not the only ones that we face. If any of the following risks occur, our business, financial condition and operating results could be negatively affected.

Because we currently derive a substantial portion of our revenues from a small number of customers, any decrease in orders from these customers could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and operating results.

We depend on a small number of customers for a substantial portion of our business, and changes in the level of our customers' orders have, in the past, had a significant impact on our results of operations. If a major customer significantly delays, reduces, or cancels the level of business it does with us, there could be an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and operating results. Significant pricing and margin pressures exerted by a major customer could also materially adversely affect our operating results. In addition, we generate significant accounts receivable from sales to our major customers. If one or more of our major customers were to become insolvent or otherwise unable to pay or were to delay payment for our products, our business, financial condition and operating results could be materially adversely affected.

We generally receive volume estimates, but not firm volume commitments from our customers, and may experience reduced or extended lead times in customer orders. Customers may cancel orders, change production quantities and delay production for a number of reasons including the use of additional suppliers. Uncertain economic and geopolitical conditions may result in some of our customers delaying the delivery of some of the products we manufacture for them and placing purchase orders for lower volumes of products than previously anticipated. Cancellations, reductions or delays by a significant customer or by a number of customers may harm our results of operations by reducing the volumes of products we manufacture and sell, as well as by causing a delay in the recovery of our expenditures for inventory in preparation for customer orders, or by reducing our asset utilization, resulting in lower profitability.

In addition, our customers may request that manufacturing of their products be transitioned from one of our facilities to another to achieve cost reductions and other objectives. Such transfers may result in short-term inefficiencies and costs due to resulting excess capacity and overhead at one facility and capacity constraints and the inability to fulfill all orders at another. In addition, we make key decisions based on our estimates of customer requirements, including determining the levels of orders that we will seek and accept, production schedules, component procurement commitments, personnel needs and other resource requirements. Changes in demand for our customers' products may reduce our ability to estimate future customer requirements accurately. This may make it difficult to schedule production and maximize utilization of our manufacturing capacity. Anticipated orders may not materialize, and delivery schedules may be deferred as a result of changes in demand for our products or our customers' products. We often increase staffing and capacity and incur other expenses to meet the anticipated demand of our customers, which causes reductions in our gross margin if customer orders are delayed or canceled. On occasion, customers may require rapid increases in production, which may stress our resources and reduce margins. We may not have sufficient capacity at any given time to meet our customers' demands. In addition, because many of our costs and operating expenses are relatively fixed over the short term, a reduction in customer demand could harm our gross margin and operating income until such time as adjustments can be made to activity and operating levels or to structural costs.

Deterioration of general economic, political, credit and/or capital market conditions could adversely affect our financial performance, our ability to grow or sustain our business, financial condition and results of operations, and our ability to access the capital markets.

CTS Corporation ("CTS", "we", "our" or "us") is a leading designer and manufacturer of products that Sense, Connect and Move. Our vision is to be a leading provider of sensing and motion devices as well as connectivity components, enabling an intelligent and seamless world. These devices are categorized by their ability to Sense, Connect or Move. Sense products provide vital inputs to electronic systems. Connect products allow systems to function in synchronization with other systems. Move products ensure required movements are effectively and accurately executed. We are committed to achieving our vision by continuing to invest in the development of products, technologies and talent within these categories.

We manufacture sensors, actuators and connectivity components in North America, Europe, and Asia. CTS provides highly engineered products to OEMs and tier one suppliers in the aerospace and defense, industrial, medical, and transportation markets, and the U.S. Government.

There is an increasing proliferation of sensing and motion applications within various markets we serve. In addition, the increasing connectivity of various devices to the internet results in greater demand for communication bandwidth and data storage, increasing the need for our connectivity products. Our success is dependent on the ability to execute our strategy to support these trends. We are subject to challenges including periodic market softness, competition from other suppliers, changes in technology, and the ability to add new customers, launch new products or penetrate new markets.

paragraphs: CTS Corporation ("CTS", "we", "our", "us" or the "Company") 為一間全球性零組件製造商，主要製造感測器、連線零組件及執行器。CTS 於 1896 年成立，為高品質電話產品供應商，並於 1929 年 2 月在印第安納州註冊為公司。本公司主要營運總部位於伊利諾州利斯爾。

我們設計、製造及銷售各式感測器、連線零組件及執行器，主要銷售對象為原廠設備製造商 ("OEMs")、航空與防禦、工業、醫療及運輸市場的一級供應商，以及美國政府。我們的願景為成為感測與運動裝置以及連線零組件的領導供應商，以實現一個智慧且無縫的世界。這些裝置依其功能被歸類為 Sense、Connect 或 Move。Sense 產品提供電子系統關鍵的輸入。Connect 產品使系統能與其他系統同步運作。Move 產品確保所需的動作能有效且精準地執行。我們致力於實現此願景，持續投資於這些類別的產品、技術及人才發展。
我們在北美、亞洲及歐洲設有製造廠。銷售與行銷透過我們的銷售工程師進行。我們也利用獨立製造商代表及經銷商來擴展銷售能力。
請參閱本年度 10-K 申報表第二部分第 8 項所包含的合併財務報表及附註，以取得有關本公司的財務資訊。
我們的產品為特定產品系列提供特定電子功能，並用於客戶組裝的產品中。下表列出了各產業的主要產品。產品銷售對象為產業 OEMs、一級供應商、經銷商及美國政府。
工業 醫療 航空與防禦 SENSE (控制、踏板、壓電感測產品、感測器，
開關、轉換器) CONNECT (電磁幹擾/射頻幹擾濾波器、電容器、頻率控制產品、電阻器、射頻濾波器)
MOVE (壓電微執行器、旋轉執行器)

我們透過銷售工程師、獨立製造商代表及經銷商向客戶進行銷售。本公司在中國、捷克共和國、丹麥、德國、日本、新加坡、臺灣及美國設有銷售辦事處。約 86% 的 2025 年淨銷售額歸因於我們的銷售工程師。
我們的銷售工程師通常服務我們最大的客戶，提供應用特定產品。我們的產品大多為工程解決方案。銷售工程師與主要客戶密切合作，設計與開發產品以符合特定客戶需求。

在 2025 年，獨立經銷商約佔淨銷售額的 7%。我們使用經銷商來處理我們產品組閤中一小部分標準化產品，這些產品需要較少的設計支援，以服務較小的客戶，並為某些客戶提供供應鏈履行服務。我們的關鍵經銷商夥伴包括大型全球及區域經銷商，例如 Avnet, Inc.、Digi-Key Electronics、Master Electronics、Future Electronics 及 TTI, Inc. 此外，我們也利用獨立製造商代表的服務，以服務未由我們銷售工程師直接服務的客戶。獨立製造商代表會向我們收取佣金以換取其服務。在 2025 年，約 7% 的淨銷售額歸因於獨立製造商代表。

CTS Corporation（"CTS"、"我們"、"我們的" 或 "我們公司"）為設計與製造 Sense、Connect 與 Move 產品的領導廠商。我們的願景是成為感測與運動裝置的領導供應商，以及連線零組件的供應商，以實現智能且無縫的世界。這些裝置根據其 Sense、Connect 或 Move 的能力進行分類。Sense 產品提供電子系統的重要輸入。Connect 產品讓系統能與其他系統同步運作。Move 產品確保所需的運動能有效且精準地執行。我們致力於實現願景，持續投資於這些類別的產品、技術與人才的發展。
我們在北美、歐洲及亞洲製造感測器、執行器及連線零組件。CTS 向航太與防衛、工業、醫療及運輸市場的 OEM 及一級供應商提供高度工程化的產品，並服務美國政府。
我們服務的各個市場中，感測與運動應用的普及程度正在不斷增加。此外，各類裝置與互聯網連線的增加，導致對通訊頻寬與資料儲存的需求增加，進而提高我們連線產品的需求。我們的成功取決於執行策略以支持這些趨勢的能力。我們面臨的挑戰包括市場週期性軟弱、來自其他供應商的競爭、技術變更，以及增加新客戶、推出新產品或進入新市場的能力。

paragraphs: 以下為可能影響本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果的風險因素。這些風險因素應與評估本年度10-K表報表或其他報送或提供之報告中所包含之預測性陳述時一併考量，因為這些因素可能導致本公司實際成果與財務狀況與預測性陳述中所預期者有重大差異。在投資本公司之前，您應知悉，進行此投資涉及風險，包括下列所描述的風險。雖然風險已按標題分類，且每項風險皆獨立討論，但許多風險之間是相互關聯的。下列所強調的風險並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。若任何下列風險發生，本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果可能會受到負面影響。
由於本公司目前來自少數客戶的收入佔有相當大的比例，因此這些客戶訂單減少可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。

本公司業務相當程度依賴少數客戶，且過去客戶訂單水準的變動對本公司營運成果產生顯著影響。若主要客戶大幅延遲、減少或取消與本公司合作的業務量，可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。主要客戶施加的重大價格與毛利率壓力也可能對本公司營運成果造成重大負面影響。此外，本公司從主要客戶銷售產生大量應收帳款。若一個或數個主要客戶無法償還或無法支付，或延遲支付本公司產品，可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大負面影響。

本公司通常會收到客戶的預估訂購量，但並非確定訂購量，且可能面臨客戶訂單減少或交貨時間延長的情況。客戶可能取消訂單、變更生產數量並延遲生產，原因包括使用其他供應商。不確定的總體經濟與地緣政治條件可能導致部分客戶延遲交付本公司為其製造的產品，並下訂較預期為低的產品數量。主要客戶或數個客戶取消、減少或延遲訂單，可能透過減少本公司製造與銷售的產品數量，以及延遲回收為應對客戶訂單所準備的存貨支出，或透過降低資產利用率，導致利潤率降低，而傷及營運成果。

此外，客戶可能要求將其產品的製造從本公司某個廠區轉移到另一個廠區，以實現成本降低及其他目標。此類轉移可能導致短暫的效率低下與成本增加，因而在某個廠區產生過度的產能與過高的營運費用，而在另一個廠區則產生產能不足與無法履行所有訂單的問題。此外，本公司根據對客戶需求的預估做出關鍵決策，包括決定將尋求與接受的訂單水準、生產排程、零組件採購承諾、人力需求及其他資源需求。客戶產品需求的變動可能降低本公司準確預估未來客戶需求的能力。這可能使本公司難以安排生產並最大化製造產能的利用率。預期訂單可能無法實現，且因客戶產品或本公司產品需求的變動，交付排程可能延後。本公司經常增加人力與產能並產生其他費用以應對客戶預期需求，若客戶訂單延遲或取消，將導致毛利率降低。有時客戶可能要求迅速提高生產，這可能使本公司資源喫緊並降低毛利率。本公司可能在任何時間點皆無足夠的產能以應對客戶需求。此外，因為許多成本與營運費用在短時間內相對固定，客戶需求減少可能傷及毛利率與營運收入，直到調整活動與營運水準或結構性成本為止。
總體經濟、政治、信用及/或資本市場條件惡化，可能對本公司財務表現、本公司成長或維持業務、財務狀況及營運成果的能力，以及本公司取得資本市場的能力產生負面影響。
